correctness.rationale: The parent-index recursion yields adjacent depth increments X_j∈{0,1}, hence H_n=h_n; D_j=d(j,j−1) is exactly 1 plus trailing two-step run. Any i<j ancestral trajectory crosses index i first at i or i−1, so d(i,j)−h_j∈{−h_i,D_i−h_(i−1)}. Since D_i=O(log i) a.s. and h_i≥(i−1)/2, the upper bounds tend to −∞, forcing only finitely many possible diameter-enhancing i. Almost-sure recurring one-step attachments fix each finite-i offset, yielding eventual equality and finite K. An initial run of 2k two-step choices produces two arms, one finite and at least length k, giving lower tail q^(2k); trailing-run union bounds give upper tail. The two-state irreducible aperiodic increment Markov chain has stationary mean 1/(1+q) and lag eigenvalue −q, giving asymptotic variance pq/(1+q)^3. Independent exhaustive choices through tree size 11 check crossing/diameter identities only, not probability-limit statements.
